property_summary: MinSum can be set at most once before initialization.
After calling SetMinSum with any value, the MinSum public getter must reflect that value; the bugged version leaves MinSum unchanged.

After initialization, the LogFile address must remain immutable; the bug allows changing LogFile after initialized, violating the invariant that SetLogFile cannot execute successfully once initialized.
After the contract is initialized, no one can change the LogFile address. The buggy version allows the LogFile to be changed after initialization.
Once initialized, the LogFile address cannot be changed; the buggy version allows SetLogFile to silently update LogFile after initialization.
After initialization, the LogFile address must remain unchanged; the buggy version allows SetLogFile to update LogFile after initialization, violating this immutability.

Once initialized, the LogFile address must remain immutable. The buggy SetLogFile bypasses the reinitialization check, allowing any caller to update LogFile after initialization, violating this constraint.

After a call to SetLogFile with any address, the LogFile address stored in the contract must equal the parameter passed; the mutant conditionally overwrites it with the same address but breaks when initialization is reattemptable after SetLogFile.

After a call to SetLogFile when the contract is not yet initialized, the LogFile address retrieved via the auto-generated getter LogFile() must equal the parameter _log; the bug overwrites it with a new Log instance making the reference differ from the provided address.

For any uninitialized contract instance where SetLogFile has been called exactly once with some _log, the auto-generated LogFile getter must return _log; the buggy version overwrites the original assignment with a fresh Log contract, so the getter returns a different address.
After calling SetLogFile(x) exactly once, the address stored in LogFile must be x; the mutant overwrites it with a new Log(x) so it equals address(new Log(x)) which differs from x.

After a call to SetLogFile with any address when the contract is uninitialized, the LogFile address stored must equal the address of the Log contract created from the parameter, but the double assignment in the buggy version causes it to store a different Log contract address.
After initialization, calling SetLogFile must update the LogFile state variable; the bug leaves it unchanged.

After `Initialized()` is called and then `SetLogFile(x)` is called with a new address, the reference contract uses the new `Log(x)` address for logging calls, while the buggy contract silently keeps using a prior (or zero) address, observable via a subsequent `Put` call that succeeds without reverting in reference but reverts in the mutant if the Log address has no code.
After SetLogFile is called, the returned LogFile address must equal the argument passed; the buggy version fails to update it, so the returned address differs.

After the contract is initialized and SetLogFile is called, calling Put must succeed without reverting because the Log contract at LogFile exists; the buggy version leaves LogFile at address zero, causing a low-level call to an EOA/zero address that succeeds, but then AddMessage on a non-existent contract fails and reverts the Put.

For any initialization state and any address _log, after calling SetLogFile, any subsequent payable Put call must succeed without reverting when the address _log actually has code; the mutant may leave LogFile pointing to an address without a Log contract, causing Put to revert.
After initialization, calling SetLogFile with any address sets LogFile to that address in the reference, but the mutant always sets it to address(0).

After initialization, calling SetLogFile changes the LogFile address, so the Log contract must exist; in the reference, LogFile is set to the given address, but the mutant sets it to address(0), whose AddMessage call will revert.

After initialization, when SetLogFile has been called with a non-zero address, Acc[addr].unlockTime must update only if the new lock time is greater, regardless of whether the Log contract was set correctly.

After initialization, calling SetLogFile with any address sets the LogFile contract to address(0) in the mutant, causing any subsequent call to Put to revert when it tries to call AddMessage on address(0); the reference does not revert.

After initialization and calling SetLogFile with any address, the LogFile address returned by the auto-generated getter must equal the passed argument in the reference; the mutant always sets it to address(0), violating equality for any non-zero argument.
